title: शब्दमञ्जरी (Sabdamanjari) — Sanskrit Noun Declension Reference
description: Structured transcription of Sabdamanjari, a companion reference to Dhaturupa Manjari from the same publisher, giving model शब्दरूप (noun/pronoun/numeral declension) paradigms with Tamil and English glosses.

source_book.publisher: Samskrit Education Society (Regd.), 148-150 (98/99) Luz Church Road, Mylapore, Chennai-600004
source_book.editions_seen_in_scan: Cover shows 4th Edition 2005; a duplicated inner title page shows 3rd Edition 2003 (First: 1986, Second: 2001, Third: 2003) — the scan appears to interleave pages from two different print runs at the very front (pp.1-2); content pagination used below follows the PDF's own physical page order.
source_book.part_of_series_note: The Tamil preface (PDF p.4) refers to this book as part of a 'सप्तमञ्जरी' (Sapta-manjari, 7-book) series alongside a Samskrit Dictionary/Samskrutasri course; compiler credited: श्री A. कुप्पुस्वामि अय्यर्.

related_files.dhaturupa_manjari_json: dhaturupa_manjari.json — companion verb-conjugation reference (same extraction project, same publisher pairing: Dhaturupa Manjari + Sabdamanjari).
related_files.vibhakti_table_json: vibhakti_table.json — a separate, pre-existing project file (used by generate_10component_quality_report.py's Śabdarūpāṇi column) with its own independently-sourced model paradigms (नारद, राम, संयुग, फल, वाल्मीकि, मुनि, रमा, गुरु, राजन्, तपस्विन्, गुणवत्, किम्/इदम्/एतद्/अस्मद्/युष्मद्). NOT derived from or synced with this extraction — several stem classes overlap (e.g. राम, मुनि, गुरु, रमा) and can be cross-checked against each other, but the two files are maintained independently; do not silently merge them.

methodology_note: Both PDFs (Dhaturupa Manjari and this one) are scanned page images with no text layer. Every entry below is a human-quality visual transcription from rendered page images (pypdfium2, scale 3.0-10.0 as needed), never OCR. Faded/ambiguous glyphs are re-rendered at higher zoom and cross-checked against the expected Paninian sandhi outcome before being accepted; any residual uncertainty is flagged in a `note` field rather than silently resolved (see e.g. section 1, word 10, सप्तमी बहुवचन, verified गोषु vs. an initial misread of गोपु).

abbreviations_used_in_book.ष. / प. (2nd occurrence, book prints bot: षष्ठी (Genitive) — the book's own abbreviation column visually prints 'प.' for both पञ्चमी and षष्ठी rows (a font/typesetting quirk, not a content error — the actual case-forms in each row are correct and distinguishable); this JSON always uses the full vibhakti name so the ambiguity does not propagate.

1_ajanta_pumlinga_sadharana.name_en: Declension of ordinary words of the Masculine Gender ending with vowels

rule_note.rule_sa_ta: मून्ऱुम् (तृतीया) विभक्तियिन् एकवचनत्तिलुम्, आऱुम् (षष्ठी) विभक्तियिन् बहुवचनत्तिलुम् 'रामेण - देवेन', 'रामाणां - देवानां' एन्ऱवाऱु ण-न माऱुपाडु कवनत्तिऱ्कुरियतु. र्, ष्, ऋ विऱ्कुप् पिन् वरुकिऱ न एऴुत्तु ण आहिऱतु; मऱ्ऱ इडत्तिल् न आहवे इरुक्किऱतु.
rule_note.rule_en: In तृतीया एकवचनम् and षष्ठी बहुवचनम् the letter न is generally changed to ण when it comes after र्, ष् or ऋ — e.g. रामेण / रामाणाम् (राम has र्, so ण), contrast देवेन / देवानाम् (देव has no र्/ष्/ऋ, so न stays unchanged). This is the णत्व rule.

words.grouping_note: एवं कपि, कवि, अतिथि, अग्नि, विधि प्रभृतयः।
एवं नृ, ज्ञातृ, शास्तृ, नेतृ, कर्तृ इत्यादयः।

words.note: No 'एवं...' grouping note is printed directly under पितृ itself; the book prints one jointly after the next word भ्रातृ ('एवं जामातृ प्रभृतयः') which — since पितृ, भ्रातृ, and जामातृ all share the identical contracted-vowel kinship declension pattern (distinct from धातृ's agent-noun pattern above) — appears intended to cover this पितृ/भ्रातृ pair as well. Flagged here rather than silently attached, per project policy on uncertain structural claims.

सप्तमी बहुवचन confirmed as गोषु after re-zooming the scan at high resolution (an initial pass at lower zoom misread the ष् glyph as प्); this matches the expected Paninian sandhi outcome (ṣ for s after the o/au diphthong). No 'एवं...' grouping note follows गो — the page ends with its संबोधनम् row and section 2 (स्त्रीलिङ्ग) begins fresh on the next page, consistent with गो being an irregular one-off paradigm in this book's list.

Only औकारान्त पुंलिङ्ग example in the book (no other औ-stem words exist to group); द्वितीया बहुवचन ग्लावः is identical in form to प्रथमा बहुवचन — read directly from scan, both print identically as 'ग्लाव:' in their respective rows.

2_ajanta_strilinga_sadharana.name_en: Declension of ordinary words of the Feminine Gender ending with vowel sounds

words.note: No 'एवं...' grouping note is printed under रमा — the page moves straight to word #13 मति. आकारान्त feminine words are common but each stem varies enough (गुण/vrddhi in वृद्धिनी-type names etc.) that this book may simply treat राम-type आकारान्त feminines as self-evident from the single model given.

words.grouping_note: एवं श्रुति, रुचि, स्मृति, बुद्धि, कीर्तिप्रभृतयः।
words.note: इकारान्त स्त्रीलिङ्ग words uniquely show two alternative forms (आ-stem vs इ-stem) in चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी/षष्ठी/सप्तमी, both printed by the book joined with a hyphen — transcribed exactly as printed, not simplified to one option.

गौरी (word 14) and नदी (word 15) are both ईकारान्त yet printed as two distinct models (द्वितीया-एकवचन गौरीम् retains long ई before म्, matching नदीं's pattern; the real contrast the book is drawing is in चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी/षष्ठी/सप्तमी, where गौरी uses only the यण्-sandhi -या/-यै/-याः/-याम् forms while नदी shows the same यण् pattern without an alternate ई-stem option, unlike मति's word 13 which explicitly gave both options) — flagged rather than asserted with full certainty, since the book gives no explicit rule text distinguishing the two beyond the two separate model tables themselves.
Like मति (word 13), धेनु shows two alternative forms (उ-stem vs. गुण-vृद्धि-stem) in चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी/षष्ठी/सप्तमी, joined by hyphen exactly as printed.

words.grouping_note: एवं चमू, श्वश्रू, तनू, जम्बू इत्यादयः (श्वश्रूः-श्वश्रूणाम्)।
words.note: Parenthetical remark '(श्वश्रूः-श्वश्रूणाम्)' printed exactly as-is by the book alongside the grouping note, apparently flagging श्वश्रू's own प्रथमा-एकवचन/षष्ठी-बहुवचन forms as worth noting specifically; transcribed verbatim rather than interpreted.

Feminine ऋकारान्त kinship words (मातृ, दुहितृ, ननान्दृ...) share the same declension shape as the masculine kinship pattern (पितृ/भ्रातृ, section 1) but with द्वितीया/षष्ठी बहुवचन ending in long-ॠ + विसर्ग/अनुस्वार (मातॄः, मातॄणाम्) rather than the masculine's ॄन्/ॄणाम् — consistent with नदी-type feminine bahuvacana not taking the masculine nasal.
No 'एवं...' grouping note — स्वसृ is given its own full model despite sharing मातृ's general kinship shape, likely because it has no true declension-twin among common words in this list.
Mirrors गो's (word 10) irregular ओकारान्त shape closely (गौः/गावौ/गावः vs द्यौः/द्यावौ/द्यावः) — द्यो being the feminine counterpart pattern. No grouping note, one-off paradigm.
Last word of section 2; section 3 (अजन्त नपुंसकलिङ्ग साधारण शब्दाः, neuter vowel-ending words) begins immediately after on the same PDF page (17), confirmed by direct read but not yet transcribed.

3_ajanta_napumsakalinga_sadharana.name_en: The words of Neuter Gender (sometimes of Common Gender also) ending with vowel sounds

general_rule_note.rule_sa_ta: (1) नपुंसकलिङ्गच् चोऱ्कळिल् पोतुवाक मुतल् वेऱ्ऱुमैयुम् इरण्डाम् वेऱ्ऱुमैयुम् ओरे माति्रियाक इरुक्कुम्; सन्दर्भत्तै ऒट्टिये पॊरुळुम् वेऱ्ऱुमैयुम् अऱियप्पालतु. (2) मून्ऱुम् वेऱ्ऱुमै मुतल् 6 वेऱ्ऱुमैकळुम् आण्पाल् चॊऱ्कळिन् वेऱ्ऱुमैकळैप् पोलवे अमैयुम्.
general_rule_note.rule_en: (1) In the case of Napumsakalinga (neuter) words, generally the Nominative case and the Accusative case (cases 1 & 2) will be the same; the meaning and case of the word should be understood from the context. (2) All the cases from the Instrumental onwards (cases 3-7) will be similar to the respective cases of words in the Masculine Gender of the same stem class.
general_rule_note.note: This is a general structural rule printed once, before word #24, governing the whole neuter-gender word list (words already given, 22-23, also conform to it, confirmed by their own tables both here).

words.grouping_note: एवं फल, धन, जन, वाहन प्रभृतयः।

words.note: Contrast with वन (word 22): नगर's bahuvacana प्रथमा/द्वितीया/षष्ठी/संबोधन end in -णि/-णाम् (नगराणि, नगराणाम्) due to the णत्व rule (न्→ण् after the stem's own र्), while वन has no र् and keeps -नि/-नाम् (वनानि, वनानाम्) — same णत्व rule already noted for देव (section 1, word 2), here shown operating word-internally rather than across a word boundary.

सप्तमी and संबोधनम् एकवचन each give two alternate forms (दधि-दधनि; दधे-दधि), confirmed at high zoom. दध्ना/दध्ने/दध्नः etc. (तृतीया-षष्ठी) show a strong-stem contraction (दधि→दध्न्) parallel to नामन्-type न्-stem nouns, not a simple i-stem pattern — flagged as a structurally distinct sub-pattern within इकारान्त नपुंसक words (contrast वारि/शुचि below, which stay closer to the plain i-stem shape).

No 'एवं...' grouping note printed — confirmed by the page ending right after वारि's संबोधनम् row and word #26 शुचि's header starting fresh, no orphaned note between them. Unlike दधि, वारि keeps a plain इ-stem throughout with णत्व (न्→ण् after र् in the stem वारि itself) rather than दधि's नकार-contraction.

शुचि ('pure') is the book's only adjective among the नपुंसक अजन्त words captured so far (contrast वारि/दधि, which are nouns) — it shows two alternate declension tracks throughout (an न्-stem track शुचिन्- alongside a plain इ-stem track शुचि-/शुचे-/शुच्य-), both given by the book and transcribed verbatim, hyphen-joined. No grouping note printed, page ends and word #27 मधु begins fresh on the next page.

rule_note.rule_sa: श्मश्रु - श्मश्रुणी श्मश्रूणि, श्मश्रुणा, श्मश्रुणः, श्मश्रुणोः श्मश्रूणाम्, श्मश्रुणि इति णत्वं विशेषः।
rule_note.rule_en: For श्मश्रु (beard), a special note: श्मश्रुणी, श्मश्रूणि, श्मश्रुणा, श्मश्रुणः, श्मश्रुणोः, श्मश्रूणाम्, श्मश्रुणि — i.e. श्मश्रु takes णत्व (न्→ण्) throughout its उकारान्त forms, because of the र् already present within the stem श्मश्र-, exactly like the general णत्व rule given earlier for देव/राम (section 1, word 2) but here triggered word-internally.

words.note: Like शुचि (word 26), मृदु ('soft') is an adjective and shows two alternate declension tracks (न्-stem मृदुन्- alongside plain उ-stem/गुण मृदो-/मृद्व-), both transcribed verbatim.

words.grouping_note: एवं नेतृ, ज्ञातृ, गन्तृ, वक्तृ इत्यादयः।
words.note: The षष्ठी/सप्तमी द्विवचन alternate form (printed after the hyphen) was hard to resolve at scan resolution even after repeated high-zoom re-renders — the visible glyph looked like 'कत्रोः' (missing the repha for र् before त्), which is not a valid form. Reconstructed here as 'कर्त्रोः', following the same short-alternate contraction pattern already confirmed directly for पितृ/भ्रातृ (section 1, words 8-9, both showing -त्रोः as their द्विवचन षष्ठी/सप्तमी contraction) — flagged per project policy rather than asserted as a confident direct read for this specific cell.

4_ajanta_pumlinga_visesha.name_en: Special/irregular masculine words ending in vowels
4_ajanta_pumlinga_visesha.part_of_book: भाग-2 विशेष शब्दाः / Section II Special Sabdas (the book's second major division, after भाग-1 'साधारण शब्दाः' = sections 1-3)

words.note: First word of भाग-2 (special/irregular words) — a patronymic showing वृद्धि (ऐ) in एकवचन/द्विवचन but गुण/mūla (इ) in बहुवचन, a genuine Paninian patronymic vṛddhi-alternation rule, not an error. The same alternation recurs at word 38 (औडुलोमि).

The book's own section header reads '३१. आकारान्तः पुंलिङ्गः निर्जर शब्दः' (ā-ending) though निर्जर itself is अ-ending like देव — transcribed exactly as printed rather than silently corrected to 'अकारान्तः'; likely refers to the word's own alternate स्-stem track (निर्जरस्-) rather than a plain vowel-ending description, or is a simple print label error. Word shows two parallel declension tracks throughout (निर्जर- and निर्जरस्-, an ancient स्-stem 'sumanas'-type alternation), both transcribed verbatim hyphen-joined; संबोधनम् एकवचन uniquely has only one form (निर्जरे, no निर्जरसे alternate), confirmed by direct zoom.

Confirmed at high zoom: पञ्चमी prints with the SAME द्विवचन/बहुवचन forms as षष्ठी in both tracks (दन्ताभ्याम्/दन्तानाम् and दतोः/दताम् — not the दद्भ्याम्/दन्तेभ्यः pattern तृतीया/चतुर्थी use), i.e. पञ्चमी and षष्ठी are printed as fully syncretized past the एकवचन row. This is unusual for a plain अ-stem (contrast पाद/यूष below, structurally parallel words which do NOT show this merge) — likely reflects दन्त's origin as a re-nominalized root-noun (मूलतः दत्) rather than a print error, but flagged here since it could not be cross-verified against a second source.

Unlike दन्त (word 32), पाद keeps पञ्चमी distinct from षष्ठी throughout (पादाभ्याम्/पादेभ्यः vs पादयोः/पादानाम्) — the standard, expected pattern, confirming दन्त's own merge is a genuine peculiarity of that specific word rather than a shared convention for this whole न्त/द्-alternation word class.

मास's alternate short track contracts all the way to मा- in the instrumental/dative/ablative द्विवचन (माभ्याम्) and बहुवचन (माभिः/माभ्यः), a stronger contraction than दन्त/पाद/यूष's alternates which keep at least a त्/द्/ष् consonant.

Same वृद्धि(strong)/गुण(weak) patronymic alternation as ऐक्ष्वाक (word 30). Two cells (षष्ठी एकवचन, सप्तमी एकवचन) print with a wrong middle consonant even after high-zoom re-render — the scan clearly and unambiguously shows 'औषुलोमेः' (ष् not ड्) and 'औहुलोमौ' (ह् not ड्), which cannot be right phonetically (ड्→ष्/ह् is not a valid sandhi anywhere in this paradigm). Corrected here to औडुलोमेः/औडुलोमौ for internal consistency with the rest of the word's own table, but the anomaly is a probable compositor error in the original book, not a misreading on this end — transcribed as corrected with this note rather than reproducing what is very likely a print defect verbatim.

rule_note.rule_sa: समासान्तगपति शब्दे भूपतिना भूपतये भूपतेः भूपतौ इति हरिशब्दवत्।
rule_note.rule_en: When पति is the LAST member of a compound (e.g. भूपति, 'lord of the earth/king'), it declines instead like हरि (section 1, word 3, a plain इ-stem) — भूपतिना, भूपतये, भूपतेः, भूपतौ — NOT with पति's own irregular पत्य्-contraction shown above, which applies only when पति stands alone.

words.note: One of the most irregular words in the book so far — प्रथमा एकवचन सखा bears no surface resemblance to the सखि stem at all (comparable to sakhi/sakhā in other Indo-Aryan reference grammars).

षष्ठी बहुवचन confirmed by direct zoom as प्रधीनाम् (standard -नाम् ending) — contrast वातप्रमी/सुधी/सेनानी below (words 42-44), which show an alternate -याम् ending for the same case, confirmed as a genuine recurring sub-pattern rather than an error (see word 42's note).

rule_note.rule_sa: किंबन्त वातप्रमी शब्दे वातप्रम्यं वातप्रम्यः वातप्रम्यि इति २-५-६-७ विभक्त्ये एकवचनेषु रूपाणि।
rule_note.rule_en: When वातप्रमी is the last member of a compound with किम् (an interrogative), its द्वितीया/पञ्चमी/षष्ठी/सप्तमी एकवचन forms shorten to वातप्रम्यं, वातप्रम्यः, वातप्रम्यि respectively.

words.note: षष्ठी बहुवचन वातप्रम्याम् (an -याम् ending, not -नाम्) confirmed by direct zoom, and independently corroborated by the same ending on सुधी and सेनानी (words 43-44) — this is a genuine recurring alternate sub-pattern for some ईकारान्त-विशेष पुंलिङ्ग words, not a print error (contrast प्रधी, word 41, which uses the plain -नाम् ending instead).

words.grouping_note: एवं सुश्री, यवक्री, शुद्धधी, परमधी इत्यादयः।

words.note: Blends an ऋकारान्त agent-noun-style strong stem (क्रोष्टा/क्रोष्टारौ/क्रोष्टारः, like धातृ/कर्तृ) with a plain उकारान्त weak stem (क्रोष्टुना/क्रोष्टुभ्याम्) — the book's own alternates in तृतीया-सप्तमी show both the ऋ-agent-noun contraction (क्रोष्ट्रा, क्रोष्ट्रे, क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्ट्रोः) and the plain उ-stem form (क्रोष्टुना, क्रोष्टवे, क्रोष्टुभ्याम्) side by side.

words.grouping_note: एवं उलू, करभू, खलपू, [अस्पष्ट], पुनर्भू, सुलू, हूहू इत्यादयः। स्त्रियामप्येवम्।

rule_note.rule_sa: हूहू हूहू शब्दस्य द्वितीया विभक्तिः इति परिवर्तते। दव्वितीये: हूहूं हूहौ हूहून्।
rule_note.rule_en: Special footnote (marked with a star): the grouped word हूहू (a Gandharva name) uniquely does NOT follow वर्षाभू's contracted-भ्व् pattern in द्वितीया — its own द्वितीया is हूहूं, हूहौ, हूहून् (a plain, uncontracted ऊ-stem shape) instead.

words.note: One name in the grouping note ('[अस्पष्ट]', transcribed provisionally, glyph unclear even at zoom — between खलपू and पुनर्भू) could not be confidently read; flagged rather than guessed. The note 'स्त्रियामप्येवम्' ('likewise in the feminine gender') states this same वर्षाभू declension pattern also applies to feminine words of the same shape.

Contrast with वर्षाभू (word 46): स्वभू uses गुण (भुव्) rather than वर्षाभू's contraction (भ्व्) in the weak forms — दो genuinely different ऊ-compound sub-patterns within the same book, both ending in -भू.

The तृतीया/चतुर्थी एकवचन and षष्ठी/सप्तमी द्विवचन cells (नरा, नरे, नरोः) were printed with a glyph that stayed ambiguous between 'न्र' and 'त्र' even after repeated high-zoom re-renders. Reconstructed here as नरा/नरे/नरोः (गुण of ऋ→अर्, the classically expected short-stem contraction for this bare ऋ root-noun) rather than asserted as a fully confident direct read — flagged per project policy.
